* Not sure which Mac you have? Click the Apple logo in the top-left corner of your screen, then click "About This Mac". If the window shows "Chip" (for example, Apple M2), choose Mac (Apple silicon). If it shows "Processor" followed by "Intel", choose Mac (Intel).

All downloads come from each company's official website.

What it costs

AI companies base their prices and usage limits on tokens, small pieces of the text the AI reads and writes. 1,000 tokens is about 750 English words. An AI agent also reads its own instructions and works through each task in several steps, so a task uses more tokens than the text you give it.

1K tokensAbout 40 short comments, or a 750-word article
10K tokensAbout 400 short comments, or a 45-minute video transcript
100K tokensAbout 4,000 short comments, or a 250-page book
1M tokensAbout 40,000 short comments, or ten 250-page books

Set up your agent

1Install itDownload it with the button above. Codex now comes inside the ChatGPT desktop app. On a Mac, open the downloaded file and drag the app into Applications. On Windows, the Microsoft Store opens: click Get.
2Sign inOpen the app and sign in with your ChatGPT account, or create one. A free account lets you try Codex; for everyday use, ChatGPT Plus ($20 a month) gives you more. Then click ChatGPT at the top of the sidebar and choose Codex. Before you send a request, check that the top of the sidebar says Codex: a chat in ChatGPT mode cannot run the commands a workflow needs, and in our test it could not even download the workflow.
3Make a folder for your workCreate a folder in your home folder, for example "AI workflows", and keep the files you want Codex to use in it. On a Mac, keep it out of Desktop, Documents and Downloads: scheduled tasks cannot open those folders. In Codex, click Choose project above the message box, then New project. Name it, click Add, pick your folder and click Create project. When Codex asks whether to trust the folder, click Trust folder: it can then read and change the files there, and it asks you before it changes files anywhere else.
4Let Codex use the internetCodex runs its commands in a protected space, the sandbox, without the internet. When a command needs the internet, such as downloading a workflow's tools, Codex asks to run it outside the sandbox. In the menu under the message box, keep Approve for me: Codex's own review then checks each request and asks you only about the ones it judges risky; approve only the workflow's own commands. Do not choose Full access, which lets Codex use the internet and change any file without asking.
5Check that it worksType List the files in this folder. The agent should reply with the names of the files inside.

Turning trend sources into a topic list

Verified Used by Misaka Studio in their company. Tested with Codex (ChatGPT app 26.1111), Claude Code (Claude app 6.6395) and DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1.
Source and terms of use Based on Sibyl System Hotspot Monitor v1.3.20 by Misaka Studio (MIT License). This version keeps its briefing format and the way it sends briefings, and changes its sources, topics and language. Not for commercial use. Used here with the author's permission, for non-commercial purposes only.

Overview

What this workflow does

Your agent sets up Sibyl, a trend monitor, for the topics you choose. Sibyl reads what is trending on Google Trends, TikTok Creative Center and Wikipedia, and on YouTube, X and Instagram if you choose them. Every hour it sends you a briefing, a short report of the strongest trends in your topics, each with a score out of 100 and one line on what it is about. When something in your topics is near the top of Google Trends, it sends an alert, a short message that arrives straight away. Sibyl finds and ranks the trends; you decide which ones to post about, and why.

Before you start
  • An AI agent that can run commands with internet access, edit files and use a web browser. One that can also run tasks on a schedule is best.
  • If you use Codex: start the chat in Codex mode and keep Approve for me, so that it can use the internet (Get set up, steps 2 and 4).
  • Node.js 18 or later on your computer. Your agent can check this and install it for you.
  • Optional: Telegram, Slack, Discord or WeCom, to receive briefings; you can use more than one. Without any, briefings are saved on your computer for 7 days.
  • Optional: accounts for some sources, such as a free TikTok for Business account for TikTok trends (step 4).
  • Optional: use AI to explain each trend in one line. Each trend in a briefing has one line saying what it is about. Sibyl normally copies a news headline for it; with this option, an AI writes it instead. This needs an API key, a code that lets Sibyl use the AI. Some AI subscriptions include one; if yours does not, buy credit on the AI company's website (for example, OpenAI's).

The scripts are free. You pay for your agent's use (reading the trend pages, one of them every hour, and answering your requests), and for X trends or an AI model if you add them.

Setup time: 1 to 4 hours in our tests, about 20 minutes of it your own stepsCost per day: the sources are free except X (about US$0.78 for 10:00 to 22:00, if you choose it), plus your agent's use
Output: a list of trends for you to review, not a posting plan First time using an agent? Set one up first →
You give the agentWhat you want to track, in your own words (for example, beauty trends in the US), your time zone and hours, and where to send briefings
You get backAn hourly briefing of the trends in your topics, each with a score, the sources it appeared on and one line on what it is about, plus alerts for the biggest ones
You still checkWhich trends fit your account, and the facts before you post. Sibyl does not catch every trend, so keep your own checks too.

Steps

Steps

  1. 1

    Choose where briefings go

    Pick one or more before you send the setup request; the tabs show what to do for each. You can change this later by asking your agent.

    Telegram: make a bot that sends you the briefings If your agent can use your browser or the Telegram app, it makes the bot and saves its token for you: open Telegram and log in when it asks. If it cannot, follow these steps. Either way, your agent then sends a test message: the new bot shows nothing until then.
    1. In Telegram, search for @BotFather and open the chat. It has a blue tick next to its name.
    2. Send /newbot. Reply with a name for your bot, then with a username that ends in "bot".
    3. BotFather replies with a token, a long line of letters and numbers. Keep it private: do not paste it into the chat. Your agent gives you a command that saves it on your computer. When you paste the token there, it does not appear; a line counts its characters. Then press Return.
    4. Open your new bot and send it any message, such as "hi". Your agent needs this message to find your chat.

    Click a screenshot to enlarge it. Account names are blurred.

    Slack: make a webhook for your channel Sibyl posts through a webhook address, a private link to one channel. If your agent can use your browser, it makes the webhook and saves it for you: log in to Slack when it asks. If it cannot, follow these steps.
    1. In your browser, open api.slack.com/apps and sign in to your workspace. The Slack app cannot make a webhook, but the briefings arrive in every Slack app.
    2. Click Create an App, then Pick features. Name it Sibyl and choose your workspace.
    3. When it asks what the app can do, add only incoming-webhook, then finish. If the last step keeps loading, reload the page: the app is already made.
    4. In the app's menu, open Incoming Webhooks, click Add New Webhook, choose your channel and click Allow.
    5. Click Copy next to the new address, paste it at the command your agent gives you, and press Return. Anyone with the address can post in your channel, so keep it out of the chat.

    Click a screenshot to enlarge it. Account names are blurred.

    Discord: make a webhook for your channel Sibyl posts through a webhook address, a private link to one channel. If your agent can use your browser or the Discord app, it makes the webhook and saves it for you: log in when it asks. If it cannot, follow these steps. Then check that its test message appears in the Discord app you use; if it does not, the channel may be in another account.
    1. In Discord, open your server and the settings of the channel for briefings (the gear next to its name). You need permission to manage the server, which you have in a server you made.
    2. Choose Integrations, then Webhooks, then Create Webhook. You can rename it Sibyl and save.
    3. Click Copy Webhook URL. The address is not shown; it is copied.
    4. Paste it at the command your agent gives you and press Return. Anyone with the address can post in your channel, so keep it out of the chat.

    Click a screenshot to enlarge it. Account names are blurred.

    WeCom: add a group robot
    1. In WeCom, open the group that should receive briefings, then the group's settings.
    2. Choose Group robot, add a new robot and name it Sibyl.
    3. Copy the webhook address it shows. Anyone with the address can post in the group, so keep it out of the chat.
    4. Paste it at the command your agent gives you and press Return.
    As in the original Sibyl, alerts can go to a second group: add a robot there as well, and tell your agent it is for alerts.

    Click a picture to enlarge it.

    No chat appNothing to set up. Briefings and alerts are saved on your computer for 7 days, and your agent shows them when you ask.
  2. 2

    Send the setup request to your agent

    Copy the request, fill in the parts in brackets, and send it to your agent.

    Setup request
    Please set up Sibyl, a trend monitor, for me. Download it from https://github.com/upiznhec/Sibyl-System-Hotspot-Monitor and follow the instructions for agents in its AGENTS.md file.

About me:
- What I want to track: [for example: beauty trends in the US, especially sunscreen]
- Country: [US]
- Time zone: [America/New_York]
- Hours to watch: [10:00 to 22:00]
- Where to send briefings (one or more): [Slack / Discord / WeCom webhook / Telegram / none, save them as files]
- Use AI to explain each trend in one line (optional, needs a paid API key): [no / yes, I have an API key]

Sources to watch:
- Google Trends: [yes / no]
- TikTok Creative Center: [yes / no]
- Wikipedia (needs a web address or email): [yes / no]
- YouTube search (free, needs a Google key): [no / yes]
- X trends (paid, needs an X developer account): [no / yes]
- Instagram (free, needs an Instagram professional account linked to a Facebook Page): [no / yes]

Before scheduling anything, show me the sources, topics, keywords, exclude words and the category you chose on each platform, and wait for my OK.
When you need something from me, such as a login, a key or a link, stop and ask me in this chat. Tell me what it is, why it is needed, whether it costs money, and where to get it.
Never ask me to paste a key or token into this chat. Give me a command that saves it on my computer.
Never type my passwords. If a page needs a login, use a browser where I am already logged in if you can; otherwise open it and let me log in myself.
If you can work in my browser and apps, do the setup steps there yourself and ask me only to log in. Keys for YouTube and X are mine to make, copy and save, and I do every step on Facebook and Instagram pages myself; give me simple steps for those.
When you are done, run the Sibyl check and a test briefing, and show me both.
    Change it for your account Fill in each part in brackets. Describe what you track in your own words; your agent turns it into topics and keywords. If you do not know your time zone's name, write your city. If you chose None in step 1, keep "none, save them as files". For "Use AI to explain each trend", write no unless you have an API key (see "Before you start"). Under "Sources to watch", Google Trends, TikTok and Wikipedia are on unless you write no. If a source needs something from you, such as a login or a key, your agent asks you when it gets there, one thing at a time, and tells you the cost and where to get it.
  3. 3

    Check the topics your agent proposes

    Before it saves anything, your agent shows a table like this one and waits for your reply. Read the keywords and exclude words, then reply "OK" or ask for changes.

    Example for "beauty trends in the US":

    PlatformProposed settingNote
    SourcesGoogle Trends, TikTok, WikipediaAs chosen in your request
    TikTokIndustry: Beauty & Personal Care, last 7 daysThe closest industry in TikTok's list
    Google TrendsCategory: Beauty and Fashion, past 24 hours. Rising searches for "skincare", "makeup" and "sunscreen"The category had only a few trends when checked
    Keywordsskincare, makeup, sunscreen, SPF (only next to "sunscreen", "skin" or "UV")You can add or remove words
    Exclude wordspromo code, couponItems with these words stay out of the briefing

    The setting on each platform decides what that platform sends; the keywords decide which of those trends count for your topic, on every platform. For a broad topic, such as world news, ask for more keywords and categories.

    Look for words that could also mean something unrelated. Ask the agent to add an exclude word, or to count a word only next to certain other words, as with SPF above. An exclude word keeps a whole trend out when any one post in it contains the word, so ask for specific words: "national football team", not "vs". Example reply: Add "lip oil", remove "makeup", and show me the table again.

  4. 4

    Log in for the sources that need it

    Google Trends and Wikipedia need no login. The sources below need you to log in, and some also need a key. Your agent asks for each one you chose when it gets there, one at a time. If it can use your browser, it opens the pages and does the clicks, except on Meta's pages; you log in, and you make, copy and save each key. If it cannot, it tells you what to click.

    TikTok: log in to TikTok for Business Without a login, TikTok Creative Center, where Sibyl reads TikTok trends, shows only the top 3 hashtags in your industry. Free.
    1. If you have no account, create a free one (sign up here).
    2. Log in once in the browser your agent reads TikTok with. If your agent can use your own browser, or bring your login over from it, it offers that first; otherwise it opens the Creative Center page in its own browser, and you log in there yourself.
    3. Nothing else to give. The login usually lasts; log in again only when your agent asks.

    Click a screenshot to enlarge it. Account names are blurred.

    Google: sign in only if Explore asks Google is replacing its Explore page, where Sibyl reads rising searches for your keywords, with one that asks you to sign in. Free.
    1. If your agent asks, sign in with your Google account, the same way as for TikTok.
    2. Or tell your agent to leave Explore out. You then lose the rising searches; Google's other lists still work.

    Click a screenshot to enlarge it. Account names are blurred.

    YouTube search: a free key from Google (optional) Finds the most-viewed new videos for your keywords. Free within Google's daily allowance.
    1. Your agent opens Google Cloud (console.cloud.google.com) in your browser, makes a project and turns on YouTube Data API v3. Any Google account works; if a school or work account sends you to its own sign-in page, as one did in testing, use another.
    2. You make the key: under Credentials, click Create credentials, then API key.
    3. Copy the key, which starts with "AIza", and paste it at the command your agent gives you.

    Click a screenshot to enlarge it. Account names are blurred.

    X trends: a paid developer account (optional) Adds what is trending on X in your country. It costs about US$0.01 per request: checking every 10 minutes from 10:00 to 22:00 costs about US$0.78 a day, and every 30 minutes about a third of that.
    1. Your agent opens the X Developer Console (console.x.com) in your browser. Sign in with your X account and set up a developer account if you have none. Check your credit balance first, and add credit yourself only if it is not enough.
    2. You make the token: create a new app, then copy its Bearer Token, which starts with "AAAA". Do not press Generate on an app you already have: it replaces that app's token and stops whatever uses it.
    3. Paste it at the command your agent gives you.

    Click a screenshot to enlarge it. Account names are blurred.

    Instagram: your own free Meta app (optional) Read this first: Meta is strict about automated activity and may lock or log out an account when a program clicks on its pages. Do every step on Meta's pages yourself; do not let your agent click there, in its browser or in yours. In testing, an agent's clicks logged Facebook out on every device. Adds top and new posts under your hashtags (up to 30) and posts taking off on accounts you choose. Free.
    1. In the Instagram app, switch to a professional account and link it to a Facebook Page.
    2. In your own browser, at developers.facebook.com, make a free app, then a token in Graph API Explorer. Your agent tells you what to click.
    3. When the pop-up asks for permissions, choose your Facebook Page and your Instagram account.
    4. Run the command your agent gives you and paste the app ID, the app secret and the token there. It turns the token into one that lasts.

    Click a screenshot to enlarge it. Account names are blurred.

    When a source needs a key, your agent gives you a command that saves it on your computer. Paste the key there: it does not appear, and a line counts its characters. Then press Return and tell your agent. Never paste a key into the chat.

  5. 5

    Check the test run and the schedule

    Your agent runs a self-check and a test briefing, and shows you both. The setup works when:

    • The self-check has no line marked MISS.
    • Collection ends with "Sibyl snapshot saved".
    • The test briefing ends with "Sibyl briefing done".

    "0 candidate(s)" in the alert check is normal. It means nothing in your topics is near the top of Google Trends at that moment.

    What your agent schedules, during your hours Every 10 minutes: Sibyl checks the sources. If you chose a chat app in step 1, it sends alerts there. Every hour: Sibyl writes a briefing. If you chose a chat app, it sends the briefing there. Every hour: your agent reads Google's trend list for your category. Once a day: it reads TikTok and Google's rising searches. The page reading runs in your agent's app, so the app must be open; after you restart the computer, open the app again. If your agent can run tasks on a schedule, it sets one up; ask to see it: "Show me the task that reads the Sibyl pages every hour." If it cannot, ask it each morning: "Read the Sibyl trend pages that are due." If you chose "none" for where to send briefings: nothing is sent. Briefings and alerts are saved on your computer for 7 days. Ask your agent when you want them, for example: "Show me the latest trend briefing." Sibyl runs on your computer: while the computer sleeps or is off, nothing is checked or sent. After a restart, the schedule starts again by itself. To get briefings while you are away, for example at night, keep the computer plugged in and awake during your hours; the screen can still turn off. On a Mac laptop, keep the lid open, open System Settings > Battery > Options and turn on "Prevent automatic sleeping on power adapter when the display is off". On a desktop Mac, turn on "Prevent automatic sleeping when the display is off" under System Settings > Energy. On Windows, open Settings > System > Power & battery and set sleep when plugged in to Never.

    On a Mac, scheduled tasks cannot read the Desktop, Documents or Downloads folders, so Sibyl has to live elsewhere, such as your home folder. If your agent asks to move it, say yes.

  6. 6

    Read your briefings

    With a chat app, a briefing arrives every hour during your hours, and alerts arrive when they happen. Without one, nothing is sent: briefings and alerts are kept for 7 days, and your agent shows them when you ask. For example:

    • "Show me the latest trend briefing."
    • "Any trend alerts today?"
    • "What were the top trends yesterday afternoon?"
    Hourly briefing (made-up example)
    Trend Briefing
Generated: 2026-11-11 10:00 EST

1. mineral sunscreen recall
Score: 87/100 (Strong)
Signals: Google Trends #1 20K+ searches, TikTok #2 73M views; on 2 sources; 2 search terms for the same event; first time in the briefing.
Summary: Brand A recalls mineral sunscreen & stick over labeling (Example News)
Links: Google Trends | TikTok

Watch list
- tinted sunscreen stick: New | Google Trends #1 +50% rising with "sunscreen"
    Alert (made-up example)
    Google Trends high-heat alert
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
mineral sunscreen recall
Rank: #1 | Heat: 20K+ searches
Summary: Brand A recalls mineral sunscreen & stick over labeling (Example News)
View details
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Trigger: heat & rank rule
Triggered at: 10:00 EST
    • Score is out of 100: Strong (85 to 100), Follow up (60 to 84), Watch (below 60). Scores and counts are a guide: Google Trends gives ranges such as "20K+", and TikTok counts cover the last 7 days.
    • Signals lists where the trend was seen, its rank and count on each source, and how it changed since the last briefing.
    • Summary is one line on what the trend is about. It comes from news headlines, or is written by an AI model if you added one. Check the facts before you use them.
    • In the real briefing, each title starts with your topic's icon and a mark for the change since the last briefing: new, rising, holding, steady or cooling.
    Change it later: requests to send your agent
    Add a topic
    In Sibyl, add a topic for [running shoes]. Propose keywords, exclude words, the matching TikTok industry and Google Trends category, and Explore keywords. Wait for my OK before saving.
    Fix an unrelated trend
    In Sibyl, "[item title]" appeared under [topic] but is not relevant. Add an exclude word or narrow the keyword, and show me what you changed.
    Change the briefing times
    Change Sibyl's briefing to [10:00, 14:00 and 18:00] only. Keep collection and alerts every 10 minutes.
    Change where briefings go
    Also send Sibyl's briefings and alerts to a [Slack] channel. Give me the command to save its webhook address on my computer, then run the Sibyl check and send a test briefing.
    Stop sending to a place
    Stop sending Sibyl's briefings to [Discord].
    Get fewer or more alerts
    Make Sibyl's alerts [stricter: only the biggest trends]. Tell me which numbers you changed.
    Turn on another source
    Turn on [YouTube search / X trends / Instagram] in Sibyl. Tell me what it costs and what I need to do, guide me one step at a time, and wait for my OK.
    Stop watching a source
    In Sibyl, stop watching [Wikipedia].
    Update Sibyl
    Update Sibyl to the latest version from GitHub. Keep my settings and keys, then run the Sibyl check and a test briefing.
    Stop Sibyl
    Stop Sibyl: remove its schedule and the page-reading task. Keep my settings, so that I can turn it on again.
    Remove Sibyl
    Remove Sibyl from this computer. Take out exactly what was set up for it, and nothing else:
1. Find the Sibyl folder you set up. If there are several Sibyl folders on this computer, work only on that one.
2. Before deleting anything, run sibyl/scripts/check-deploy.js there and note which places and keys were set up (names only, never the values).
3. Remove its schedule: in that folder, run node sibyl/scripts/schedule.js --remove (on Windows, delete its two Task Scheduler tasks). If your app blocks this, give me the command to run in my terminal.
4. Delete the task, reminder or loop you made in your own app to read Sibyl's pages. Close the browser you started for Sibyl, and stop anything you started to keep the computer awake for it.
5. Delete the Sibyl folder, with its settings, saved keys, briefings, logs and browser profile. Keep Node.js: other programs may use it.
6. Check that nothing is left: no Sibyl block for that folder in the schedule (crontab -l on a Mac), no Sibyl task in your app, and no folder.
7. Tell me what you removed, and list the bots, apps, webhooks and keys that still exist in my accounts (Telegram, Slack, Discord, WeCom, Google Cloud, X or Meta), with how to delete each one.

If it goes wrong

If it goes wrong

From the original Sibyl's notes and from our tests with Codex, Claude and DeepSeek (November 2026). More are added as testers report them.

While setting up

Your agent cannot reach the internet
What it looks like: The Sibyl check shows "Internet access" as MISS, every source fails with "ENOTFOUND", or Codex cannot download Sibyl. Your agent may offer a script for you to run instead.What to do: In Codex, start a new chat in Codex mode (the top of the sidebar says Codex), keep Approve for me, and send the request again. Codex then asks to run each command that needs the internet outside its sandbox (Get set up, steps 2 and 4). In other apps, allow internet access for your agent. Then ask your agent: "Run the Sibyl check again."
Your agent asks you to paste a key into the chat
What it looks like: It asks you to send a YouTube key, an X token or a webhook address as a message.What to do: Do not paste it. Reply: "Give me the command that saves it on my computer." Run that command and paste the key where it asks. The key does not appear; a line counts its characters. Press Return, then tell your agent it is saved. If you already pasted a key, make a new one and save that instead.
You pasted a key, but your agent says it is not saved
What it looks like: You pasted the key at the command and told your agent, but the Sibyl check says it is not set.What to do: Go back to the terminal. If the line under the question shows the characters received, press Return there. If it says "Nothing pasted yet", copy the key again, paste it and press Return. Then tell your agent.
You have to log in again in your agent's browser
What it looks like: You are logged in to TikTok or Google in your own browser, but your agent opens its own browser and asks you to log in there.What to do: To make a key or buy credit, use your own browser: your agent only needs the saved key. TikTok is different, because your agent reads it every day. Ask: "Can you use my browser, or bring my login over?" If not, log in once in its browser, or skip the login and get the top 3 hashtags only. If it set up your chat apps in its own browser, ask it afterwards to sign out of the sites it no longer needs.
Your agent asks you to run a script it wrote
What it looks like: Instead of setting up the schedule itself, the agent writes its own setup script and asks you to run it in Terminal.What to do: Do not run it. Reply: "Use Sibyl's own schedule script, as AGENTS.md says." On a Mac, if your agent asks to move the Sibyl folder out of Desktop, Documents or Downloads, say yes: scheduled tasks cannot read those folders.
Your agent cannot find your Telegram chat
What it looks like: Your agent says it found no message from you, although you opened your bot.What to do: Send your bot a message such as "hi". In testing, pressing Start was not enough. Then tell your agent.
Facebook logs you out during the Instagram setup
What it looks like: After your agent opened Meta's developer pages in its own browser, Facebook asked you to log in again on every device.What to do: Log in again in the Facebook app on your phone and confirm that it is you. Then do the Meta steps in your own browser, while your agent tells you what to click.
Your agent cannot find your Instagram account
What it looks like: The token is saved, but your agent finds no Facebook Page or Instagram account.What to do: Check that your Instagram account is a professional account linked to the Page. In Graph API Explorer, make a new token and choose your Page and Instagram account in the pop-up, then run the command your agent gave you again.

After setup

Briefings do not arrive in your chat
What it looks like: Your agent can show the briefings, but nothing arrives in your chat app.What to do: Ask your agent: "Run the Sibyl check and send one test briefing." The check lists every place briefings go. If one fails, make a new webhook or token there and save it with the command your agent gives you. If the check says they were sent, your agent may have set the place up in another account signed in to the browser it used; in testing, a second Discord account had a server of the same name. Tell your agent which account you use, or show it your app.
Your computer restarted or lost its internet connection
What it looks like: No briefing arrives for a while, or your agent says it could not read a page.What to do: After a restart, open your agent's app again. The schedule starts again by itself; runs missed while the computer was off or asleep are not made up. If your agent reads pages in a browser of its own, it opens it again at its next reading; if it says it cannot, ask: "Open your browser again and read the Sibyl pages that are due." After a network drop there is nothing to fix: the next run reads the sources again. Briefings made while nothing could be sent are kept on your computer for 7 days: "Show me the Sibyl briefings I missed."
Each briefing arrives twice
What it looks like: The same briefing or alert arrives two times.What to do: Ask your agent: "Check Sibyl's scheduled tasks for duplicates." Only Sibyl's own scripts should send messages; a schedule should only start them.
Briefings arrive at the wrong times
What it looks like: Briefings start or stop an hour or more away from your hours.What to do: Tell your agent your city and your hours. It checks the schedule against your computer's time zone and sets it again.
The briefing shows trends unrelated to your topic
What it looks like: "Sheltered inlets" led a beauty briefing. It came from Google's rising searches for "sunscreen", which Sibyl reads for your topic.What to do: Sibyl now puts such items in the watch list at the end, unless one of your keywords or a second source confirms them. If one still leads, ask your agent: "In Sibyl, [trend] is not relevant. Add an exclude word and show me what you changed."
Alerts about sports matches in a news topic
What it looks like: In a world affairs topic, alerts such as "japan vs paraguay" arrive. In testing, 9 of 12 alerts in one day were matches.What to do: Country names in your keywords are also the names of national teams. Ask your agent: "Tie the exclude word 'vs' to the country keywords in Sibyl, not to the whole topic." A word tied to one keyword stops only that keyword from matching, so other news about the country still arrives.
The same trend appears in every briefing
What it looks like: A trend stays in briefing after briefing.What to do: Nothing, while it is still trending: the mark before its title shows whether it is new, rising, holding, steady or cooling. To leave it out, ask your agent to add an exclude word for it.
Your agent wants to drop a page that works in your browser
What it looks like: Your agent says that a Google or TikTok page keeps failing and suggests leaving it out, but the page opens normally for you.What to do: Ask your agent: "Compare what the page shows with what your reader expects before dropping it." In testing, an agent blamed Google for seven hours; the cause was its own reader, and it found it within a minute once it compared the two.
Your agent stopped Sibyl before you asked
What it looks like: When your hours end, your agent removes the schedule or its page-reading task on its own. Briefings can keep arriving while the pages are no longer read.What to do: Tell your agent: "Do not stop anything until I ask. When I do, stop the schedule and the page reading together." When you want Sibyl to stop, send the Stop Sibyl request under "Change it later".
How experienced users check
  • Run the same prompt in a second agent and compare the results.
  • Work out whether the problem is the prompt or the service.
  • Fix it one step at a time with follow-up instructions.
  • Ask the agent where each fact came from, then check the source.

Sorting comments into themes

Being tested [Which agents it was tested with, and when, will go here after testing]
Source and terms of use This workflow is adapted from comment-mining (version 1.0.0), a free skill published by ScrapeCreators under the MIT License. We kept its comment categories, its themes and its report layout. We added scripts that do the counting and check every quote, and the option to read your own posts through each platform's official API. We are not affiliated with ScrapeCreators. Our scripts are open source too: comment-themes (MIT License).

Overview

What this workflow does

You give your agent the links to some posts, yours or someone else's. It reads all the comments, groups them into themes (questions, complaints, praise, people who want to buy, and so on) and writes a short report. The report says how many people raised each theme and quotes what they actually wrote. The comments are saved on your computer, so you can come back later and ask about them.

Before you start
  • An AI agent that can use the internet and work with files on your computer. If you don't have one yet, see Get set up.
  • Node.js 20 or later. Your agent can check whether you have it and install it if not.
  • Nothing else for now. Some platforms need a key or a connection, and your agent will walk you through it the first time you need one (step 3).

The scripts are free, and so is reading comments through the platforms' official APIs, except on X, which charges for each reply it reads. Other people's posts and Reddit go through ScrapeCreators, a paid service: about 1 credit for every 10 to 20 comments, and you get 100 credits free. You also pay for your agent, as usual.

[Setup time, measured during testing][Cost of one analysis, measured during testing]
It only reads and reports. It never replies or posts. First time using an agent? Set one up first →
You give the agentLinks to the posts, and whether they're yours. YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, X and Reddit all work.
You get backA short report on what people are saying, with numbers and real quotes, plus a spreadsheet of every comment and the theme it was put under.
You still checkWhether the themes make sense for your audience, and any quote before you reuse it. Comments on a few posts don't tell you what a whole market thinks.

Steps

Steps

  1. 1

    Choose your posts

    Choose whose posts they are, then paste the links below. You can paste as many as you like, from any mix of platforms.

    Whose posts are these?

    If you have both, do them as two separate requests.

    These are examples. Replace them with your own links.
        How do you want your own posts read?

        This only applies to your own Instagram, Facebook and TikTok posts. Other people's posts on these platforms always go through ScrapeCreators. You can skip this, and your agent will ask you later.

        Official APIScrapeCreators
        Cost Free, except X, which charges up to about 1.5 US cents for each reply it reads. About 1 credit for every 10 to 20 comments, so a post with 100 comments takes about 5 to 10 credits. You get 100 credits free, no card needed.
        Setup More work. You create keys or an app, and some platforms only work with a professional account. Easy. One key from scrapecreators.com works for Instagram, Facebook, TikTok and Reddit.
        Whose posts On most platforms, only your own. YouTube and X let you read anyone's. Anyone's, as long as the post is public.
        Risk None. It's the platform's own access. It isn't the platform's own access, so it doesn't always work. On Instagram, about 1 read in 10 fails.
        Details for each platform: access, limits and prices

        This is what we found when we checked in November 2026. Each company sets its own prices and limits and can change them at any time, so check their own pages before you pay for anything. Any charges are between you and that company.

        YouTube
        YouTube Data API. Free, with an API key you create in Google Cloud. You get 10,000 units a day, and reading up to 100 comments uses 1 unit. It works for any public video.
        Instagram
        Instagram API, through a Meta app you create yourself. Free. It needs an Instagram professional account (business or creator) linked to a Facebook Page you manage, and it only reads that account's posts. Commenters' usernames are included.
        Facebook
        Facebook Pages API, through the same Meta app. Free. It only reads posts on Pages you manage, not personal profiles. While your Meta app is in development mode, other people's comments come without their names.
        TikTok
        TikTok's official connector for AI apps. Free, and it works with personal accounts: you sign in with TikTok, and the permission lasts a year. It only reads your own videos. On a video with more than 500 comments, the rest come sorted by likes and some may repeat.
        X
        X API, paid from credit you buy at console.x.com: about US$0.005 for each post or reply it reads, plus US$0.010 for each different person. There are no automatic top-ups. Posts of any age can be read. For posts older than 7 days it uses X's full-archive search, which is included when you pay per use.
        Reddit
        This workflow reads Reddit through ScrapeCreators only.
        ScrapeCreators
        A paid service that reads public posts on many platforms. Each request that returns data costs 1 credit (a page of about 10 to 20 comments), and failed requests are free. New accounts get 100 credits with no card, and credits don't expire; for example, 25,000 credits cost US$47. By their own figure, Instagram reads succeed about 9 times in 10. On Instagram, TikTok and Facebook, replies are counted but not read.
        How each post is read
        PlatformYour postsOther people's
        YouTube Official APIfree Official APIfree
        Instagram Official APIScrapeCreators ScrapeCreators
        Facebook Official APIPages onlyScrapeCreators ScrapeCreators
        TikTok Official connectorScrapeCreators ScrapeCreators
        X Official APIpaid Official APIpaid
        Reddit ScrapeCreators ScrapeCreators
        • The platform's official API (free, except X)
        • ScrapeCreators (paid, works for any public post)
        • Grayed-out rows and columns aren't part of your request.
      • 2

        Send the request to your agent

        Copy this and paste it into your agent. The first time, do it in an empty folder: your agent will set everything up there before it starts. After that, keep using the same folder.

        Request
        
              
        
            
        
            
        
              
        
                What's in the request
                The first line tells your agent to set the workflow up if it isn't there yet, so you can use the same kind of request every time.
                The last lines ask it to go one step at a time, to never ask you to paste a key or password into the chat, and to tell you what anything costs before it spends money.
              
        
            
        
          
        
        
        • 

        
      • 
          
        3
        Answer what your agent asks
        
          
        
            
        
              
        Your agent will only ask for what it still needs, one question at a time.
        
              
        
                The first time you use a platform
                
          
                  
        • It may need a key or a connection for that platform. For ScrapeCreators, YouTube and X, if your agent can use the browser you're already logged in to, it opens the pages and does the clicks. You only log in, then make and copy the key. Instagram and Facebook need your own Meta app, and there you do every click yourself. TikTok needs its connector added to your AI app.
          • 
                  
        • It gives you a command that saves the key on your computer. You never paste a key into the chat.
          • 
                  
        • If you didn't choose how to read your own Instagram, Facebook or TikTok posts, it asks you once and remembers your answer.
          • 
                
        
              
        
              
        
                Every time
                
          
                  
        • Before it reads anything that costs money, it tells you how many comments each post has and what reading them will cost, and waits for your OK.
          • 
                  
        • If it can't match a link to your Facebook Page, it shows your Page's latest posts and asks which one you meant.
          • 
                
        
              
        
            
        
            
        
              
        
                On Meta's websites
                Do every click on Facebook, Instagram and Meta for Developers yourself. When a program clicks there, Meta may log you out, ask for ID or restrict the account. If that happens, stop and tell your agent.
              
        
              
        [Screenshots of making and saving a key, added after testing]
        
            
        
          
        
        
        • 

        
      • 
          
        4
        Read the report
        
          
        
            
        
              
        Once the comments are in, your agent sorts them and writes the report. It lists the main themes and how many people mentioned each, then the questions people asked, their doubts, signs that they want to buy, phrases worth reusing and ideas for new content. It also saves a spreadsheet of every comment with its theme, so you can check or filter them yourself.
        
              
        [A real report from the tests, added after testing]
        
            
        
            
        
              
        
                How the numbers are checked
                Your agent decides the theme of each comment, but a script does the counting, so the numbers aren't guesses. Another script checks that every quote in the report really appears in the comments.
                If a post has more than 1,000 comments, only its 1,000 most-liked are analyzed, and the report says so.
              
        
            
        
          
        
        
        • 

        
      • 
          
        5
        Ask your own questions
        
          
        
            
        
              
        Since the comments are saved on your computer, you can ask about them whenever you like. Your agent answers with real counts and the matching comments, not guesses. To pick up new comments, ask it to read the posts again.
        
              
        
                
        Count a topic
        How many people asked about the price?
        
                
        See every comment on a theme
        Show me every complaint about shipping, with the comment IDs.
        
                
        Find people to reply to
        List who asked where to buy, so I can reply to them.
        
                
        Pick up new comments
        Read the same posts again to pick up new comments.
        
              
        
              
        
                Change it later: requests to send your agent
                
        
                  
        Switch how your own posts are read
        From now on, read my own [Instagram / Facebook / TikTok] posts through [ScrapeCreators / the official route] in the comment themes workflow. Tell me what I need to set up, guide me one step at a time, and wait for my OK.
        
                  
        Replace a key
        My [ScrapeCreators / YouTube / X / Meta] key for the comment themes workflow has changed. Give me the command that saves the new one on my computer, then check that it works.
        
                  
        See how much credit is left
        Check my comment themes keys. Tell me how many ScrapeCreators credits I have left, and how many posts I have read on X in this billing cycle.
        
                  
        Read more of a big post
        Not every comment on [post link] was read. Tell me how many more you can read and what that costs, and wait for my OK.
        
                  
        Sort every comment of a big post
        Sort every comment on [post link] into themes, not only its 1,000 most-liked. Tell me first how many comments that is, and wait for my OK.
        
                  
        Combine posts in one report
        Put the comments from [my last two requests / all comments posted in the last 30 days] into one report, sorted into themes.
        
                  
        Update the workflow
        Update the comment themes workflow to the latest version from GitHub. Keep my keys, choices, comments and reports, then run its tests.
        
                  
        Remove the workflow
        Remove the comment themes workflow from this folder. Show me what you would delete and wait for my OK. Then tell me where to remove each key and connection.
